questions.prompt: t0 = now(); launch(...); t1 = now(); reports 4 µs for a big kernel. Why?
options: Launches are asynchronous: it measured only the time to queue the launch

questions.prompt: Why discard the first few runs?
options: The first launch loads the kernel's code and clocks ramp up, so early runs don't represent steady state

questions.prompt: 30 runs: 29 take about 10 µs, one takes 300 µs. Which summary best describes typical performance?
questions.explanation: The median ignores the outlier; the mean doesn't.

questions.prompt: A kernel takes 1 µs on the GPU, and each launch costs the host 4 µs. Back to back, what fraction of the time is the GPU busy, in %?
questions.explanation: One kernel per 4 µs, 1 µs of which is work.

options: Batching work into fewer, bigger launches
questions.explanation: The kernel isn't the bottleneck; the launches are.

questions.prompt: Why interleave A and B runs when comparing two versions?
options: Slow drifts (temperature, clocks, other load) then affect both equally
questions.explanation: Otherwise drift shows up as a false difference.
